projects.name: End-to-end Bitcoin prediction pipeline
projects.blurb: A production data pipeline that runs every morning with no one touching it: it ingests BTC prices and crypto headlines into a BigQuery warehouse, transforms them with dbt, orchestrates with Airflow, and serves daily predictions to a live dashboard. The model behind it is one I built from scratch, and the dashboard is honest that it doesn't beat guessing.

showcase.title: BTC prediction pipeline
showcase.text: Personal project · 2026 · Live dashboard The production system around a model I'd already built: ingestion, a warehouse, transformations, orchestration, inference, and serving. Every day it pulls yesterday's Bitcoin close and a few hundred crypto headlines, scores the headlines, rebuilds the features, predicts where BTC lands 3 days out, and publishes the call. Swapping in a better model later is one file and a rerun.

showcase.title: Production pipeline
showcase.text: Production pipeline: daily ingestion into a BigQuery warehouse (raw, staging, and marts layers), dbt transformations, and a 7-task Airflow 3 DAG run on GitHub Actions. Inference is a NumPy-only forward pass, so production needs no GPU, and a FastAPI dashboard on Render serves the results.

showcase.title: Built to fail loudly
showcase.text: Built to fail loudly: idempotent merges on every load, a guard that refuses to predict on stale features, and a post-run check that fails the workflow if no fresh prediction landed. When my Snowflake trial ended mid-build, I moved the warehouse to BigQuery without changing how data flows.

showcase.title: Live results
showcase.text: Live results: 690 predictions backfilled and tracked daily. As of Sep 2026 the model hits 49.6% vs. 52.5% for always predicting "up", inside the ±3.7-point margin of error. The dashboard shows this next to every prediction.

showcase.title: The model it serves
showcase.text: The model it serves: an LSTM with no model.fit(). Every gate, gradient, and weight update is written by hand in CuPy (Xavier init, BPTT, gradient clipping), and I found and fixed four silent gradient bugs along the way.

showcase.title: Sentiment model
showcase.text: Sentiment model: fine-tuned CryptoBERT on 59k+ relabeled news headlines, taking macro-F1 from 0.39 to 0.79 with a market-impact labeling rubric and 500 targeted synthetic examples. The model and dataset are public on Hugging Face.

showcase.title: Features
showcase.text: Features: 27 engineered features (RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, ATR, VWAP, SPY/DXY returns, sentiment rolling averages), pruned to 22 by removing pairs correlated above 0.95.

showcase.title: Rigor
showcase.text: Rigor: a purged chronological 70/15/15 split with a horizon-length gap. An early 0.551 accuracy turned out to be selection bias from early stopping on test data, and retraining properly exposed it.

showcase.title: Finding
showcase.text: Finding: five independent checks (logistic regression, gradient boosting, and three LSTM setups) all land at the no-information baseline. Technical indicators plus sentiment don't predict 3-day BTC direction, and I can show it with numbers.

showcase.title: Performance at a glance
showcase.text:
Clean holdout: 51.5% direction accuracy vs. 51.8% majority baseline (606 rows).

Pipeline backfill: 49.6% hit rate vs. 52.5% always-up baseline (687 scored predictions; September 24, 2026).

The Bitcoin direction model did not beat either baseline.

projects.name: DrawADigit: a neural net from scratch
projects.blurb: Draw a digit in the browser and a network I built in pure NumPy/CuPy classifies it in real time. No ML libraries.

showcase.title: DrawADigit
showcase.text: Personal project · Live demo A handwritten-digit recognizer built from scratch using only NumPy and CuPy, served behind a live web demo.

showcase.title: 97.32% test accuracy
showcase.text: 97.32% test accuracy on MNIST (60,000 training images, 10,000 test images).

showcase.title: Architecture
showcase.text: Architecture: 784 → 128 → 64 → 10, ReLU hidden layers, softmax output, categorical cross-entropy.

showcase.title: No ML libraries
showcase.text: No ML libraries: the forward pass, backpropagation, and mini-batch gradient descent are all written by hand.

showcase.title: Deployed
showcase.text: Deployed: a FastAPI backend in Docker with a browser canvas frontend.

showcase.title: Performance at a glance
showcase.text: 97.3% MNIST test accuracy

projects.name: Shakespeare autocomplete: RNN vs. LSTM
projects.blurb: A character-level language model trained on Shakespeare's complete works. Type a seed phrase and it writes the rest.

showcase.title: Shakespeare autocomplete
showcase.text: Personal project · Live demo A character-level language model trained on the complete works of Shakespeare. Enter a seed phrase, pick a model, and it generates a continuation one character at a time, with a temperature slider for creativity.

showcase.title: Architecture
showcase.text: Architecture: Embedding (64) → 2-layer SimpleRNN or LSTM (256 units) → softmax over a 50-character vocabulary, with a 40-character sliding window.

showcase.title: Found a silent bug after deploying
showcase.text: Found a silent bug after deploying: the vocabulary came from an unordered Python set, so training and inference used different character mappings. Building it from a sorted list fixed it.

showcase.title: RNN vs. LSTM
showcase.text: RNN vs. LSTM: the SimpleRNN plateaued at 51% val accuracy (loss 1.60), a visible case of vanishing gradients. Swapping in an LSTM reached 56% (loss 1.47) and converged in 7 epochs instead of 12.

showcase.title: Deployed
showcase.text: Deployed: a FastAPI backend in Docker with a live browser demo.

showcase.title: Performance at a glance
showcase.text: 56% LSTM val acc · RNN 51%
